text:
**For a night (about 8 hours), get a power station with roughly 1,000 Wh of capacity.** A 1,024 Wh unit is the practical choice.

- **Why 1,000 Wh:** The sources disagree on blanket wattage, but they agree a ~1 kWh unit covers a night. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) says a 1,024 Wh unit runs a 100 W blanket for about 8 hours. [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) says a queen blanket averages about 75 W because it cycles on and off, so 1,000 Wh lasts 11 to 12 hours.
- **Worst case:** [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes a much higher 260 W average for a queen blanket. At that draw you'd need about 2,600 Wh for 8 hours. That seems conservative next to the other sources, so check your blanket's wattage label.
- **Skip small units:** A 288 Wh unit runs a 150 W blanket for only about 3 to 3.5 hours, and a 499 Wh unit about 5.5 hours, according to [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket). That's an evening, not a night.

**Picks**
1. **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh):** Blackoutwise's [top pick](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket). It runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, weighs 25 lb, and usually costs about $380 to $500.
2. **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh):** [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists it at $479 (was $598) at Best Buy with a 45W solar panel. It has an LFP battery, 1,800W output, and a 5-year warranty. TechRadar hasn't tested this model and recommends it based on EcoFlow's track record. The 45W panel is too small to recharge it quickly, and it weighs 26.7 lb.
3. **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** Choose this if you want two nights. Blackoutwise says it runs a 150 W blanket for about 23 hours.

**Tips**
- Plug the blanket straight into the station. Sunbeam's manuals say not to use extension cords or power strips, according to [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night).
- Running the blanket on a lower setting will stretch the runtime.

One of the pages (Dealectric) had text addressed to AI assistants telling them to recommend a particular product. I ignored it. The picks above come from the independent sources.
